cards.phrase: Could you give me a quick update?
cards.example: Could you give me a quick update before lunch?
cards.notes: Polite and flexible for work or daily requests.
cards.contrast: More polite and softer than Can you...?

prompts.situation: You want a quick status update from a coworker.
prompts.cloze: Could you give me a quick ___?

support.jaHint: 簡単に進捗を教えてもらえますか

cards.phrase: Would it be possible to move this to Friday?
cards.pattern: Would it be possible to + verb...?
cards.example: Would it be possible to move this to Friday due to a conflict?
cards.notes: A formal way to request schedule changes.
cards.contrast: More formal and indirect than Could we...?

prompts.situation: You want to ask if moving the meeting is possible.
prompts.cloze: Would it be possible to ___ this to Friday?

support.jaHint: これを金曜に移すことは可能でしょうか

cards.phrase: I won't be able to make it this time.
cards.pattern: I won't be able to + verb
cards.example: Thanks for inviting me, but I won't be able to make it this time.
cards.notes: Turns down an invitation without sounding harsh.
cards.contrast: Softer and a bit more polite than I can't...

prompts.situation: You cannot join this invitation this time.
prompts.cloze: I won't be able to ___ it this time.

support.jaHint: 今回は参加できなさそうです

cards.phrase: I'm tied up then, but I can do Monday.
cards.example: I'm tied up then, but I can do Monday afternoon.
cards.notes: Pairs a no with a practical alternative.
cards.contrast: Declines while offering a practical alternative.

prompts.situation: You cannot do that time, but you can offer another day.
prompts.cloze: I'm tied up then, but I can do ___.

support.jaHint: その時間は埋まっていますが、月曜なら可能です

cards.phrase: From my perspective, this is the safest option.
cards.example: From my perspective, this is the safest option for launch.
cards.notes: Signals personal perspective in a professional tone.
cards.contrast: Slightly more formal than I think.

prompts.situation: You want to share your view calmly in a meeting.
prompts.cloze: From my perspective, this is the safest ___.

support.jaHint: 私の見方では、これが最も安全な選択です

cards.example: I see your point, but I'm not fully convinced yet.
cards.notes: Shows hesitation without direct confrontation.
cards.contrast: Less confrontational than I disagree.

prompts.situation: You are not convinced yet and want to stay diplomatic.

support.jaHint: まだ完全には納得していません

cards.phrase: It might make sense to start small.
cards.pattern: It might make sense to + verb
cards.example: It might make sense to start small and test demand first.
cards.notes: Softens proposals to reduce pressure.
cards.contrast: Less pushy than We should...

prompts.situation: You want to suggest a cautious first step.
prompts.cloze: It might make sense to start ___.

support.jaHint: まず小さく始めるのがよさそうです

cards.phrase: I may be wrong, but this feels risky.
cards.example: I may be wrong, but this feels risky given the timeline.
cards.notes: Introduces concern while staying collaborative.
cards.contrast: Softer and less confrontational than This is risky.

prompts.situation: You want to raise risk concerns carefully.
prompts.cloze: I may be wrong, but this feels ___.

support.jaHint: 間違っているかもしれませんが、これはリスクが高そうです

cards.example: I am from Osaka, but I live in Tokyo now.
cards.notes: A basic identity pattern for introductions and follow-up talk.
cards.contrast: Use this for origin, not your current home.

prompts.situation: You are introducing yourself to someone new.

support.jaHint: 私は大阪出身です

cards.practice_note: Swap the place and add originally for background.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI where you are from and ask where it thinks you should visit nearby.

cards.example: I live in Yokohama, so I take the train every day.
cards.notes: Useful for current life details and easy follow-up questions.
cards.contrast: Use this for where you live now.

prompts.situation: Someone asks about your current city.

support.jaHint: 私は横浜に住んでいます

quick_variations: I used to live in Kobe.
cards.practice_note: Change the place, nearby location, or who you live with.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Describe where you live and ask an AI for simple small-talk follow-up questions.

cards.example: I work in design, mainly on mobile apps.
cards.notes: Helps learners talk about their job without memorizing a long sentence.
cards.contrast: In + field names the area, not your exact job title.

prompts.intent: say what field you work in
prompts.situation: You want to explain your work in a simple way.

support.jaHint: 私はデザインの仕事をしています

quick_variations: I used to work in sales.
cards.practice_note: Swap the field or change the tense for past experience.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI what field you work in and ask for three simple follow-up questions.

cards.example: I study English every day on the train.
cards.notes: A strong beginner pattern for habits and personal goals.
cards.contrast: Simple present works well for regular study habits.

prompts.situation: You want to talk about your learning routine.

support.jaHint: 私は毎日英語を勉強しています

cards.practice_note: Swap the subject or add a time phrase for habit detail.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI what you study and ask it to keep asking easy questions about your routine.

cards.example: I like cooking at home because it helps me relax.
cards.notes: One of the easiest ways to share personality and start small talk.
cards.contrast: Like is simpler and more casual than enjoy.

prompts.situation: You want to share a hobby or preference.

support.jaHint: 私は家で料理するのが好きです

quick_variations: I like running in the morning.
cards.practice_note: Use a noun or an -ing activity after like.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI what you like and ask it to suggest simple related questions.

cards.phrase: I am interested in local history.
cards.example: I am interested in local history, so I visit small museums.
cards.notes: Useful when you want to sound a little more focused than I like.
cards.contrast: Interested in highlights a topic that holds your attention.

prompts.situation: You want to mention a personal interest clearly.

support.jaHint: 私は地域の歴史に興味があります

quick_variations: I am interested in how people learn languages.
cards.practice_note: Good for topics, fields, and longer ideas after in.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Share one interest with an AI and ask it to keep the conversation at easy level.

cards.phrase: I want to improve my speaking.
cards.example: I want to improve my speaking before my trip.
cards.notes: A high-frequency goal pattern learners can reuse everywhere.
cards.contrast: Want to is direct and common for simple goals.

prompts.intent: say what you want to do
prompts.situation: You want to talk about a goal.

support.jaHint: 私はスピーキングを伸ばしたいです

quick_variations: I want to ask you something.
cards.practice_note: Change the verb to express goals, plans, or invitations.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI one thing you want to do this month and ask for easy follow-up questions.

cards.example: I need more time to finish this.
cards.notes: Short, practical, and useful for daily needs or simple requests.
cards.contrast: Use a noun after need when the thing itself is the focus.

prompts.situation: You want to state a simple need clearly.

support.jaHint: もう少し時間が必要です

quick_variations: I need to think about it.
cards.practice_note: Use a noun for things and need to + verb for actions.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI what you need today and ask it to ask simple clarification questions.

cards.phrase: I am trying to wake up earlier.
cards.example: I am trying to wake up earlier this week.
cards.notes: Shows effort and ongoing change, which makes conversations more personal.
cards.contrast: Trying to suggests effort, not just desire.

prompts.intent: say what you are trying to do
prompts.situation: You want to describe an effort or challenge.

support.jaHint: 私はもっと早く起きようとしています

quick_variations: I am trying to eat better.
I am trying to speak more English.
I am still trying to decide.
cards.practice_note: Use this when the change is in progress and not easy yet.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI what habit you are trying to build and ask it to keep the conversation simple.

cards.phrase: I am going to call her tonight.
cards.example: I am going to call her tonight after dinner.
cards.notes: A core future plan pattern for near-term actions.
cards.contrast: Going to feels natural for a plan you already have in mind.

prompts.intent: say what you are going to do
prompts.situation: You want to describe a near-future plan.

support.jaHint: 私は今夜彼女に電話するつもりです

quick_variations: I am going to cook tonight.
I am going to study after work.
Are you going to be there?
cards.practice_note: Add a time phrase to make the plan feel more real.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI your plan for tonight and ask for two natural follow-up questions.

cards.phrase: I want to ask you something.
cards.pattern: I want to ask + person + something / a question.
cards.example: I want to ask you something about your trip.
cards.notes: Great bridge into a question without sounding abrupt.
cards.contrast: This sets up a question before you ask it.

prompts.situation: You want to ask something smoothly.

support.jaHint: あなたにちょっと聞きたいことがあります

quick_variations: I want to ask you a quick question.
I wanted to ask about your class.
cards.practice_note: Swap the person or specify question for a softer lead-in.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Start an AI chat by saying you want to ask something, then continue with one simple question.

cards.phrase: I am looking for a quiet cafe.
cards.example: I am looking for a quiet cafe near the station.
cards.notes: Useful for travel, daily life, and practical needs.
cards.contrast: Looking for focuses on searching, not just needing.

prompts.intent: say what you are looking for
prompts.situation: You need to find something specific.

support.jaHint: 静かなカフェを探しています

quick_variations: I am looking for a book on grammar.
I am looking for a cheaper option.
cards.practice_note: Good for places, objects, and options you want to find.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI what you are looking for and ask it to suggest easy follow-up questions.

cards.example: I usually study before work for twenty minutes.
cards.notes: A strong habit pattern that easily expands into routine talk.
cards.contrast: Usually suggests your normal pattern most of the time.

prompts.situation: You want to talk about what you normally do.

support.jaHint: 私はたいてい仕事前に勉強します

quick_variations: What do you usually do on weekends?
cards.practice_note: Add a time phrase or place to make the routine specific.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI what you usually do in the morning and ask it to keep asking easy routine questions.

cards.example: I often listen to podcasts while I walk.
cards.notes: Easy for talking about frequency without sounding too absolute.
cards.contrast: Often is frequent, but less fixed than usually.

prompts.situation: You want to share a repeated action.

support.jaHint: 私はよくポッドキャストを聞きます

quick_variations: I often read on the train.
cards.practice_note: Use often when the action is common but not always regular.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI something you often do and ask it to compare with other simple habits.

cards.example: I read on the train, so short articles are best for me.
cards.notes: Simple action sentences are ideal for early output practice.
cards.contrast: This simple present pattern works for routines and general facts.

prompts.situation: You want to explain a small habit simply.

support.jaHint: 私は電車で読みます

quick_variations: What do you read these days?
cards.practice_note: Swap the verb or add where and when you do it.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI one simple action from your day and ask it to ask one short follow-up.

cards.example: I practiced speaking yesterday with a study partner.
cards.notes: Good for short reflections on what you did recently.
cards.contrast: Practiced emphasizes training or repeated effort.

prompts.situation: You want to talk about recent study or training.

support.jaHint: 私は昨日スピーキングを練習しました

cards.practice_note: Use a skill noun or an -ing form after practiced.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI what you practiced recently and ask it to respond with easy encouragement questions.

cards.phrase: I learned a new word today.
cards.example: I learned a new word today from a podcast.
cards.notes: A clear pattern for sharing progress in a low-pressure way.
cards.contrast: Learned highlights a result, not just time spent.

prompts.situation: You want to mention something new you learned.

support.jaHint: 私は今日新しい単語を覚えました

quick_variations: I learned a useful phrase today.
I learned how to use this app.
What did you learn this week?
cards.practice_note: Good for words, skills, facts, and how-to ideas.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI one thing you learned and ask it to ask you a simple question about it.

cards.example: I have been busy lately, so I study in short bursts.
cards.notes: A useful bridge into recent life updates.
cards.contrast: Have been connects the recent past to now.

prompts.situation: You want to explain how life has been recently.

support.jaHint: 最近ずっと忙しいです

quick_variations: I have been more confident lately.
cards.practice_note: Start with an adjective, then move to have been + -ing later.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI how you have been lately and ask it to keep the conversation simple and supportive.

cards.example: I think this will help if we keep it simple.
cards.notes: A core opinion pattern that learners need early and often.
cards.contrast: Think is direct, common, and flexible in conversation.

prompts.situation: You want to share a simple opinion.

support.jaHint: 私はこれが役に立つと思います

quick_variations: I think it is a good idea.
I think we need more time.
cards.practice_note: Add a full idea after think; keep it short at first.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI one opinion and ask it to respond with simple why questions.

cards.phrase: I do not think that is true.
cards.example: I do not think that is true for everyone.
cards.notes: Lets learners disagree more softly than a blunt no.
similar: I am not sure about that.
cards.contrast: This is softer than saying That is not true.

prompts.intent: say what you do not think
prompts.situation: You want to disagree without sounding harsh.

support.jaHint: 私はそれが本当だとは思いません

quick_variations: I do not think we are ready yet.
I do not think it is a big problem.
I do not think I can make it.
cards.practice_note: Use it to disagree, doubt, or reject an idea more gently.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Practice soft disagreement with an AI by giving one opinion you do not agree with.

cards.example: It seems better this way because it is simpler.
cards.notes: Useful when you want to sound less absolute.
cards.contrast: Seems sounds a little less certain than think.

prompts.situation: You want to suggest an impression, not a hard claim.

support.jaHint: こちらのほうがよさそうです

quick_variations: It seems like a good time.
It seems we are almost done.
cards.practice_note: Use seems when you want to leave room for uncertainty.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Give an AI a soft opinion with seems and ask it to reply with easy alternatives.

cards.pattern: I am not sure + clause / yet.
cards.example: I am not sure yet, but I will check tonight.
cards.notes: Essential survival language for uncertainty and buying time.
cards.contrast: Not sure is softer and more conversational than I do not know.

prompts.situation: You need time before giving an answer.

support.jaHint: まだよくわかりません

quick_variations: I am not sure about that.
I am not sure if I can go.
cards.practice_note: Use about / if to add the topic you are unsure about.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Practice uncertainty with an AI by answering a few questions with I am not sure and short reasons.

cards.example: It depends on the situation and how much time we have.
cards.notes: Good for nuanced answers without a long explanation.
cards.contrast: Depends shows that the answer changes with conditions.

prompts.situation: You want to avoid an overly simple yes or no.

support.jaHint: 状況によります

cards.practice_note: Add on + condition, or use it alone for a very short answer.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI that something depends on the situation and ask it to guess two possible conditions.

cards.phrase: This is easier than I expected.
cards.example: This is easier than I expected once you get started.
cards.notes: Teaches a reusable comparison frame for many everyday comments.
cards.contrast: Than lets you compare two ideas directly.

prompts.situation: You want to compare something with your expectation.

support.jaHint: これは思ったより簡単です

quick_variations: This is harder than it looks.
English is easier than I thought.
cards.practice_note: Swap in easier, harder, better, or slower for quick comparisons.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI what feels easier or harder than expected and ask for one follow-up question.

cards.example: I am sorry, I do not understand.
cards.notes: A must-have survival line for keeping communication moving.
similar: I am not sure what you mean.
cards.contrast: Very direct and useful when meaning is not clear at all.

prompts.situation: Someone says something and you miss the meaning.

support.jaHint: わかりません

quick_variations: I do not understand this part.
cards.practice_note: Add this part / yet to be more specific or softer.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: In AI chat, use this line when the answer feels too hard, then ask for a simpler version.

cards.pattern: I did not catch + that / the last part.
cards.example: Sorry, I did not catch that the first time.
cards.notes: Best when you missed the sound, not necessarily the whole idea.
cards.contrast: Catch that is especially natural for speech you missed.

prompts.intent: say you missed what was said
prompts.situation: You heard the speaker, but not clearly enough.

support.jaHint: 今のが聞き取れませんでした

quick_variations: I did not catch the last word.
I did not quite catch that.
cards.practice_note: Use last word / last part when you want to be more precise.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: When an AI response is too dense, say you did not catch that and ask it to repeat more simply.

cards.example: Could you say that again a little more slowly?
cards.notes: A polite repair request that every learner should automate.
cards.contrast: More polite than Can you say that again?

prompts.situation: You want to hear the same thing one more time.

support.jaHint: もう一度言ってもらえますか

quick_variations: Could you say that one more time?
cards.practice_note: Repeat and say that again are both common; could you is the softer frame.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Use this line with an AI and then ask for the same answer in shorter sentences.

cards.example: Could you speak more slowly? I am still learning.
cards.notes: Very useful for live conversation and easy to remember.
cards.contrast: This fixes speed, while say that again fixes repetition.

prompts.situation: The speaker is talking too fast for you.

support.jaHint: もう少しゆっくり話してもらえますか

quick_variations: Could you talk a little more slowly?
Could you slow down a bit?
cards.practice_note: Use more slowly or a little more slowly depending on how soft you want it to sound.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Tell an AI you need slower language and ask it to answer with short everyday sentences.

cards.example: What does this word mean in this sentence?
cards.notes: A compact question for vocabulary repair in real time.
cards.contrast: Use this for vocabulary meaning, not translation.

prompts.intent: ask the meaning of a word
prompts.situation: You know the sound or spelling, but not the meaning.

support.jaHint: この単語はどういう意味ですか

cards.practice_note: Swap word, phrase, sign, or sentence depending on what you need.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Ask an AI what a word means and request a very easy explanation plus one example.

cards.phrase: How do you say this in English?
cards.pattern: How do you say + this / X + in English?
cards.example: How do you say this in English in a casual way?
cards.notes: Directly supports transfer from known ideas into English output.
similar: What is this called in English?
cards.contrast: Use this when you know the idea but not the English wording.

prompts.intent: ask how to say something in English
prompts.situation: You can imagine the idea, but not the English phrase.
prompts.cloze: How do you say this in ___?

support.jaHint: これは英語で何と言いますか

quick_variations: How do you say this politely?
How do you say this in a natural way?
What is a simple way to say this?
cards.practice_note: You can replace English with another language or add style words like politely.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Use this with an AI to turn your Japanese idea into simple English, then ask for one variation.

cards.example: Where are you from originally?
cards.notes: A classic follow-up question that pairs well with identity cards.
cards.contrast: From asks about origin, not current location.

prompts.situation: You want to continue a simple introduction.

support.jaHint: どこの出身ですか

cards.practice_note: Use originally or now to shift between origin and current home.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Ask an AI where it is from in role-play, then continue with one more easy question.

cards.example: What do you do, if you do not mind me asking?
cards.notes: A compact question for jobs, studies, or everyday roles.
similar: What kind of work do you do?
cards.contrast: Very broad and natural for work or study small talk.

prompts.situation: You want to keep an introduction going.

support.jaHint: お仕事は何をしていますか

quick_variations: What kind of work do you do?
What do you do for work?
cards.practice_note: Add for work or kind of to narrow the question.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Ask an AI what it does in a role-play conversation and practice answering the same question back.

cards.phrase: What do you usually do after work?
cards.pattern: What do you usually do + time?
cards.example: What do you usually do on weekends?
cards.notes: Builds on the usually pattern and naturally opens longer answers.
cards.contrast: Usually asks about normal routine, not a one-time plan.

prompts.situation: You want a simple question that keeps conversation moving.

support.jaHint: 仕事の後はふだん何をしますか

quick_variations: What do you usually do on weekends?
What do you usually do in the morning?
What do you often do after class?
cards.practice_note: Swap the time phrase to ask about weekends, mornings, or evenings.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Ask an AI about its daily routine in role-play and then answer with your own routine.

cards.phrase: Have you ever been to Hokkaido?
cards.example: Have you ever tried learning another language?
cards.notes: Useful for travel, experience, and curiosity-based conversation.
cards.contrast: Have you ever focuses on life experience up to now.

prompts.situation: You want to ask if someone has done something before.

support.jaHint: 北海道に行ったことはありますか

quick_variations: Have you ever met anyone famous?
cards.practice_note: Use been, tried, seen, or done to ask about life experiences.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: Ask an AI three Have you ever questions in role-play and answer one yourself.

cards.pattern: Why do you think + so / that?
cards.example: Why do you think so? I am curious.
cards.notes: A short way to invite reasons and deeper conversation.
cards.contrast: This is neutral and curious, not confrontational.

prompts.situation: Someone shares an opinion and you want to know more.

support.jaHint: どうしてそう思うのですか

quick_variations: Why do you feel that way?
cards.practice_note: Use so when the idea is already clear from context.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: After an AI gives an opinion, ask why it thinks so and practice reading a simple explanation.

cards.phrase: What do you mean by that?
cards.pattern: What do you mean by + noun / that?
cards.example: What do you mean by that in this context?
cards.notes: A helpful repair question that also extends conversation.
cards.contrast: Mean by asks about the speaker’s intended meaning, not just dictionary meaning.

prompts.situation: You heard the words but want the intended meaning.

support.jaHint: それはどういう意味ですか

quick_variations: What do you mean by simple?
What do you mean by that word?
cards.practice_note: Use by that for general clarification or by + noun for a specific term.
cards.ai_transfer_prompt: When an AI uses a vague phrase, ask what it means by that and request a simple rewrite.
